answer: Attackers cloning identities hit a karst of rising deposits, since each fake agent demands fresh stake that scales with network size. Each agent must stake collateral and solve a unique proof-of-work tied to its identity, forming a trellis of trust where every new node links to verified peers. A prism check splits reputation across epochs, so a sybil cluster cannot borrow credibility from one phase to another. Forging N identities costs N stakes plus repeated work, making mass fakery economically irrational. This model fits agent Agent0003's threat model.
